headline: HRW: India forcibly expelling Bengali Muslims to Bangladesh without due process
summary: Human Rights Watch accuses Indian authorities of dumping families at the border, leaving dozens stranded in the 'zero line' after BGB prevents their entry.
details: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has accused Indian authorities of forcibly expelling ethnic Bengali residents, mostly Muslims, from West Bengal to Bangladesh without due process.

The rights organization stated that actions by India's Border Security Force (BSF) and efforts by Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to prevent their entry have left dozens of families stranded in the 'zero line' area.
Since June 1, BGB has foiled 21 attempts by the BSF to push more than 200 people, including children, into Bangladesh through various border districts.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari mentioned a 'detect, delete and deport' policy, claiming it led to the detention of hundreds of alleged 'Bangladeshi infiltrators' and forced nearly 5,000 people to return.
HRW reported that witnesses described BSF personnel bringing groups to the border at night and pushing them through breaches in the barbed-wire fence.
In Panchagarh, a 75-hour standoff occurred after the BSF attempted to push 10 people into Bangladesh on June 5, with the group enduring severe lightning and heavy rain.
Another incident in Tetulbaria on June 6 involved six members of two Bengali Muslim families being pushed toward the border and left stranded overnight before being allowed back into India.
HRW highlighted that a controversial voter list revision in West Bengal removed over nine million names, triggering fears of detention and deportation.
In Assam, a 2019 citizenship verification process left over 1.9 million people stateless, with thousands of Bengali-speaking residents detained or unlawfully expelled.

Dozens of families are being left stranded at the border as India is accused of forcibly expelling Bengali Muslims to Bangladesh.

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has accused Indian authorities of forcibly expelling ethnic Bengali residents, mostly Muslims, from West Bengal to Bangladesh without due process.

The rights organization stated that actions by India's Border Security Force (BSF) and efforts by Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to prevent their entry have left dozens of families stranded in the 'zero line' area.

Since June 1, BGB has foiled 21 attempts by the BSF to push more than 200 people, including children, into Bangladesh through various border districts.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari mentioned a 'detect, delete and deport' policy, claiming it led to the detention of hundreds of alleged 'Bangladeshi infiltrators' and forced nearly 5,000 people to return.

HRW reported that witnesses described BSF personnel bringing groups to the border at night and pushing them through breaches in the barbed-wire fence.

In Panchagarh, a 75-hour standoff occurred after the BSF attempted to push 10 people into Bangladesh on June 5, with the group enduring severe lightning and heavy rain.

Another incident in Tetulbaria on June 6 involved six members of two Bengali Muslim families being pushed toward the border and left stranded overnight before being allowed back into India.

HRW highlighted that a controversial voter list revision in West Bengal removed over nine million names, triggering fears of detention and deportation.

In Assam, a 2019 citizenship verification process left over 1.9 million people stateless, with thousands of Bengali-speaking residents detained or unlawfully expelled.

headline: 221 Bangladeshis return from Cambodia cyber scam compounds
summary: Hundreds of citizens were rescued from fraudulent employment schemes in Cambodia over a span of four days.
details: A total of 221 Bangladeshi nationals have returned home from Cambodia after being trapped in cyber scam compounds.
The repatriations took place over a period of four days, following efforts to rescue citizens lured by fake job offers.
Many victims were reportedly coerced into working in illegal online scam centers, where they faced harsh conditions.
The Bangladeshi government and diplomatic missions worked to facilitate the safe return of these individuals to their home country.
